The starting point

Explore how to integrate a language model into an application while preserving information traceability. The goal is to answer questions about known documents and help a person review where each statement comes from.

How I built it

  • Closed ES/EN library: three original website notes and a demo guide, with stable sections and links.
  • Lightweight queries from the start: lexical retrieval and verbatim excerpts in the browser, without downloading a model.
  • Optional AI with Qwen3.5 and WebLLM: voluntary download, a separate worker and on-device processing.
  • The application links the generated paragraph to its source and the excerpt used, keeping identifiers, links and evidence under its control.
  • Insufficient information when evidence is missing; no internet search, private files or action execution.
  • If the device is incompatible or generation fails, lightweight queries remain available. Controls stop the model and clear its download.

The result

A bilingual prototype for trying context retrieval and reviewing an answer alongside its evidence. The case explains integration decisions and system boundaries without claiming commercial outcomes or accuracy metrics.

Public evaluation: questions, sources and results

What it checks. What still needs review.

  • A citation must exist in the library and its excerpt must match. That alone does not demonstrate that the model’s interpretation is correct.
  • Retrieval looks for matching words and bounded concepts. It can miss differently phrased questions; this is not semantic search with embeddings.
  • Lightweight queries show verbatim excerpts, not generated answers. The optional model is small and can make mistakes; review its sources.
  • The model needs WebGPU, a download of about 450 MB and available graphics memory. It may not work on some phones. There are no API charges; downloads can use your connection’s data allowance.

Cookies and privacy

What we store

The at_consent cookie remembers your choice for six months. Optional settings are stored locally for the same period. You can withdraw permission here: those settings will be deleted. Controls still work during your visit if you choose necessary only. If you enable the demo’s optional AI, the browser may store model files; delete them from the demo itself. Questions are not stored. The booking calendar connects to Cal.com only when you open it; booking details are handled under that provider’s privacy policy.

When you submit the form, your name, email, subject and message pass through Formspree to reach alejandro.dev.sergio@outlook.com. They are used to respond to your enquiry. The provider processes and stores details under its privacy policy. Do not include passwords or sensitive information.
